entities.summary:
Ulderico Carpegna was an Italian Cardinal and jurist born in unknown year, died on January 24, 1679. He played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church's governance during the late 17th century.

As a prominent figure in the Curia Romana, Carpegna participated in several key events, including the conclave that elected Pope Innocent XI in 1676 and contributed to the development of the papal state's administration. His influence extended beyond Italy, as he collaborated with other high-ranking clergy and European monarchs.

Carpegna's legacy is marked by his efforts to modernize the Church's administrative structures and promote its interests globally. He played a crucial role in shaping the Catholic Church's stance on various issues, including the Protestant Reformation and the rise of nation-states.

The Italian jurist's remarkable journey spans centuries, with his name etched into the annals of history as a champion of the Catholic faith.
